function.description: Send a GET request to a specified URL to retrieve all products and branches with triangulation runs in the latest 90 days. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request as a dictionary of header names to header values.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

end_date.description: The end date for the data retrieval period, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If null, defaults to the current date.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the request.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to a certificate file to verify the peer.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names to cookie values.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary mapping protocol names to URLs of the proxies.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.content:
**Triangulation Metrics** refers to a set of quantitative measures used to evaluate the quality, reliability, and performance of triangulation processes—typically in contexts such as geographic information systems (GIS), computer vision, robotics, or data fusion. These metrics help determine how accurately multiple observations or sensors can be combined to estimate a point’s position, orientation, or other properties.

Key aspects often covered by triangulation metrics include:

| Metric | What it Measures | Typical Use |
|--------|------------------|-------------|
| **Accuracy** | Difference between estimated and true positions. | Assess overall precision of the triangulation system. |
| **Precision** | Variability of repeated estimates under identical conditions. | Evaluate consistency and repeatability. |
| **Uncertainty Ellipse/Volume** | Statistical confidence region around the estimate. | Visualize spatial uncertainty. |
| **Dilution of Precision (DOP)** | Effect of geometry on measurement accuracy. | Common in GPS/RTK systems. |
| **Baseline Length & Angle** | Distance and relative orientation between observation points. | Influence geometric strength of triangulation. |
| **Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)** | Quality of raw measurements. | Predict potential errors. |
| **Residuals / Goodness-of-Fit** | Difference between observed and modeled data. | Detect outliers or systematic biases. |
| **Coverage / Redundancy** | Number of independent observations per target. | Ensure robustness against failures. |
| **Computational Complexity** | Time/memory required for processing. | Optimize real‑time applications. |

In practice, triangulation metrics guide decisions such as sensor placement, algorithm selection, and error mitigation strategies. They are essential for validating results, comparing different triangulation methods, and ensuring that the derived positions meet the required standards for safety, navigation, or scientific research.
